note: One of six property tax notices added 2026-08-27 to give the `propertytax` sub_bill_type (commercial-narrative-v11) real coverage across municipalities -- before them the corpus held no tax notice at all, while that family accounted for 21 of the 26 misrouted payables in the B2 audit. sub_bill_type 'propertytax' is the assertion these documents exist for: measured 6/6 on a scratch analyzer, both twins agreeing at 0.858-0.892, with controls held (burnaby_water->water, business_license->business_license, bchydro->electric). City of Richmond 2026 PROPERTY TAX NOTICE. total 2,041.65 printed 4x and the largest figure on the page. payment_due_date from 'DUE DATE: Thursday, July 2, 2026'. || invoice_date is deliberately NOT asserted: this page prints NO issue-date label at all (no Invoice/Billing/Statement/Notice/Issue Date), so build_write_values substitutes date.today() and the run wrote 2026-08-27. `regress.py --add` proposed it as 'stable' only because all three replicates ran on the same day -- a false green that would flip red tomorrow. The defaulting itself is the open A1/A6 defect class, not something this sidecar should lock in. payment_due_date IS asserted because the page prints it explicitly. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice.
